body.text: auṃ / saha nāv avatu / saha nau bhunaktu / saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai / tejasvi nāv adhītam astu / mā vidviṣāvahai /
body.translated_text: <s>Auṃ</s>. May He protect us both. May He nourish us both. May we both work together with vigor. May our study be brilliant. May we not quarrel with each other.

children.translated_text: Chapter One
<s>Hariḥ Oṃ</s>. Those who discourse on <s>Brahman</s> say:

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ brahma kutaḥ sma jātā
children.translated_text: What is the cause? [Is it] <s>Brahman</s>? Whence are we born?
By what do we live? And on what are we established?
Governed by whom do we live in pleasures and pains,
O knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, [following] the ordained course?
Time, inherent nature, necessity, chance,
the elements, the womb, <s>Puruṣa</s> — these are to be considered.
The combination of these [is not the cause], nor even the self [alone],
for the self too is powerless regarding the cause of pleasure and pain.
Those who followed the path of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>yoga</s> perceived
the power of the divine self (<s>devātma-śakti</s>), hidden by its own qualities (<s>guṇas</s>).
He who presides over all those causes —
time, self, and the rest — He alone [rules them all].
Him [they perceived as] having one rim, threefold, with sixteen ends,
fifty spokes, twenty counter-spokes,
six sets of eight, one bond of manifold form,
with three paths distinguished, and one delusion arising from two causes.
[We meditate on that <s>Brahman</s> as] a river of five streams, fierce and crooked, from five sources,
whose waves are the five <s>prāṇas</s>, whose root is the fivefold <s>buddhi</s>,
with five whirlpools, a torrent of five pains,
with fifty divisions and five branches.
In this vast wheel of <s>Brahman</s>, which encompasses all living beings and is the abode of all,
the individual soul (<s>haṃsa</s>) wanders about.
Knowing oneself as distinct from the Impeller,
favored by Him, one attains immortality.
This has been sung as the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,
and in it are the triad and the imperishable, firmly established.
Knowing the inner [reality] therein, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>
become merged in <s>Brahman</s>, devoted to That, freed from the womb [of rebirth].
The Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) sustains this entire [universe], conjoined —
the perishable and the imperishable, the manifest and the unmanifest.
And the self, not being lord, is bound due to the state of being an experiencer;
but knowing God (<s>deva</s>), one is freed from all bonds.
There are two unborn ones — the knower and the unknower, the lord and the non-lord.
There is [another] unborn one, connected with the experiencer, the object of experience, and purpose.
And the self is infinite, of universal form, and a non-doer.
When one discovers this triad, that is <s>Brahman</s>.
The perishable is <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter); the immortal and imperishable is <s>Hara</s> (Śiva).
The one God (<s>deva</s>) rules over both the perishable and the self.
By meditating on Him, by union [with Him], and by contemplating the true nature of reality,
there is, further, at the end, the cessation of all cosmic illusion (<s>viśva-māyā</s>).
By knowing God, [there is] the falling away of all bonds;
with afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) destroyed, [there is] the cessation of birth and death.
By meditating on Him, [there is] a third [state] upon the dissolution of the body —
universal sovereignty; alone, with all desires fulfilled.
This is to be known — that which eternally abides in the self.
There is nothing higher than this to be known.
Knowing the experiencer, the object of experience, and the Impeller,
all has been declared — this is the threefold <s>Brahman</s>.
Just as the form of fire, when latent in its source,
is not seen, and yet its essential nature (<s>liṅga</s>) is not destroyed —
it can be seized again from the fire-source by means of kindling —
so indeed, both [aspects] are [realized] in the body by means of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ).
Making one's own body the lower fire-stick (<s>araṇi</s>),
and <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) the upper fire-stick,
by the practice of the churning of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>),
one sees God, as [fire] hidden [in wood].
As oil in sesame seeds, as butter in curds,
as water in river-beds, and as fire in fire-sticks,
so the self is grasped within the self
by one who perceives it through truth and austerity (<s>tapas</s>).
The all-pervading self,
as butter permeating milk,
rooted in self-knowledge and austerity —
that is <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme teaching of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>.
That is <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme teaching of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>.
Thus ends the first chapter.
Chapter Two
First yoking the mind
to the truth, <s>Savitṛ</s> [yoked] his thoughts;
discerning the light of fire,
he brought it forth from the earth. [*1]

children.text: [*1] This mantra is also found in Yajurveda 11.1.

children.translated_text: With yoked mind, we,
by the impulsion of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>,
with power [strive] for heaven. [*2]

children.text: [*2] This mantra is also found in Yajurveda 11.2.

children.translated_text: Yoking the gods with the mind,
those who go to heaven by thought, to the luminous realm —
he who will create a great light,
<s>Savitṛ</s> impels them. [*3]

children.text: [*3] This mantra is also found in Yajurveda 11.3

children.translated_text: They yoke the mind and they yoke the thoughts,
the inspired sages of the great, the wise one.
He alone who knows the ordinances has arranged the priestly functions —
great is the praise of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>. [*4]

children.text: [*4] This mantra is also found in Yajurveda 11.4, 5.14, and Rigveda 5.81.1.

children.translated_text: I yoke your ancient prayer (<s>Brahman</s>) with salutations;
may [my] verse go forth on the path, like the sun.
May all the sons of the immortal hear,
they who have attained the celestial abodes. [*5]

children.text: [*5] This mantra is also found in Yajurveda 11.5 and Rigveda 10.13.1.

children.translated_text: Where fire is kindled,
where the wind is controlled,
where <s>Soma</s> overflows —
there the mind is born.
Through the impulsion of <s>Savitṛ</s>,
one should delight in the ancient <s>Brahman</s>.
If you make your source there,
then your past [karma] will not taint you.
Holding the body upright with the three [upper parts] erect and even,
drawing the senses and the mind into the heart,
the wise one should cross, by the boat of <s>Brahman</s>,
all the fear-bearing currents.
Compressing the breaths here, with movements controlled,
when the breath is exhausted, one should breathe out through the nostrils.
Like a chariot yoked with unruly horses,
the wise one should restrain the mind without negligence.
On a level, clean [place], free from pebbles, fire, and sand,
devoid of disturbing sounds, water pools, and the like,
pleasing to the mind and not painful to the eyes,
in a sheltered cave, protected from the wind — there one should practice [<s>yoga</s>].
Mist, smoke, sun, wind, fire,
fireflies, lightning, crystal, and the moon —
these are the preliminary forms
that manifest <s>Brahman</s> in <s>yoga</s>.
When the fivefold quality of <s>yoga</s> arises,
produced from earth, water, fire, wind, and space,

children.text: na tasya rogo na jarā na mṛtyuḥ
children.translated_text: for one who has attained a body made of the fire of <s>yoga</s>,
there is no disease, no old age, no death.
Lightness, health, freedom from craving,
clarity of complexion, excellence of voice,
pleasant smell, and scantiness of urine and excrement —
these they declare to be the first signs of <s>yoga</s> practice.
Just as a mirror stained with dirt,
when well-cleaned, shines brilliantly,
so the embodied one, seeing the true nature of the self (<s>ātma-tattva</s>),
becomes one, purpose-fulfilled, freed from sorrow.
When by the true nature of the self, the truth of <s>Brahman</s>
is perceived here, as if by the light of a lamp, by the one who is disciplined —
knowing God as unborn, eternal, purified of all categories of existence,
one is freed from all bonds.
This God indeed [pervades] all the quarters;

children.text: pūrvo ha jātaḥ sa u garbhe antaḥ
children.translated_text: He was born before [all], and He is within the womb.
He alone was born, and He is to be born [in future];
He stands facing all beings in every direction.
The God who is in fire, who is in the waters,
who has entered the whole world,
who is in the plants, who is in the trees —
to that God, salutation upon salutation!
Thus ends the second chapter.
Chapter Three
He who alone, possessing the net [of <s>māyā</s>], rules with His ruling powers,
who rules all the worlds with His ruling powers,
He who alone [presides] at their arising and their coming together —

children.text: ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
children.translated_text: those who know this become immortal.

children.text: eko hi rudro na dvitīyāya tasthur
children.translated_text: For <s>Rudra</s> is one alone; they do not stand for a second.
He who rules these worlds with His ruling powers,
He stands facing all beings and, having created [all], withdraws [them] at the end of time,
having projected all worlds, the Protector.
Having eyes everywhere, having faces everywhere,
having arms everywhere, having feet everywhere,
He forges [them] together with His arms and with wings,
the one God, generating heaven and earth.

children.text: [*7] This mantra is also found in Yajurveda 17.19 and Rigveda 10.82.3.

children.translated_text: He who is the origin and the arising of the gods,
the lord of all, <s>Rudra</s>, the great seer (<s>maharṣi</s>),
who produced <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo) in the beginning —
may He endow us with auspicious understanding (<s>buddhi</s>).
O <s>Rudra</s>, that form of Yours which is auspicious (<s>śiva</s>),
non-terrifying, revealing no evil —
with that most benign body of Yours,
O Dweller on the mountain (<s>Giriśanta</s>), appear to us! [*8]
O Dweller on the mountain (<s>Giriśanta</s>), the arrow
which You hold in Your hand to cast,
O Protector of the mountain (<s>Giritra</s>), make it auspicious;
do not harm any person or living being. [*9]
Higher than that is <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme, the great,
hidden in all beings according to their bodies,
the one who envelops the whole universe —
knowing the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), they become immortal.
I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s>,
of the color of the sun, beyond darkness.
Only by knowing Him does one pass beyond death;
there is no other path for going [to liberation]. [*10]
Than whom there is nothing higher, nothing whatsoever,
than whom there is nothing smaller nor anything greater,

children.text: vṛkṣa iva stabdho divi tiṣṭhaty ekas
children.translated_text: He stands like a tree, firmly fixed in heaven, the One —
by that <s>Puruṣa</s> is all this filled.
That which is higher than this,
that is formless and without affliction.
Those who know this become immortal;
but the others go only to suffering.
He whose faces, heads, and necks are everywhere,
who dwells in the cave [of the heart] of all beings,
who is all-pervading — He is the Blessed Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>);
therefore He is the all-pervading, auspicious one (<s>Śiva</s>).
The great Lord indeed is <s>Puruṣa</s>,
the impeller of the highest consciousness (<s>sattva</s>).
This most pure attainment —
the Lord (<s>Īśāna</s>) is the imperishable light.
The <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the measure of a thumb, is the inner self (<s>antarātmā</s>),
always seated in the heart of beings.
He is fashioned by the heart and the mind, by thought —

children.text: ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
children.translated_text: those who know this become immortal.
The <s>Puruṣa</s> of a thousand heads,
of a thousand eyes, of a thousand feet,
having enveloped the earth on all sides,
He stood ten fingers' breadth beyond.
<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this —
what has been and what is to be.
He is also the lord of immortality,
which He transcends through [providing] food. [*12]
With hands and feet everywhere,
with eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,
with ears everywhere in the world,
He stands, enveloping all.
Reflecting the qualities of all the senses,
yet devoid of all the senses,
the lord and ruler of all,
the great refuge of all,
In the city of nine gates, the embodied one,
the swan (<s>haṃsa</s>), moves about outwardly,
the controller of the entire world,
of all that is stationary and moving.
Without hands or feet, yet swift and grasping,
he sees without eyes, he hears without ears;

children.text: sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasyāsti vettā
children.translated_text: he knows all that is to be known, yet none knows him —
they call him the foremost, the great <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great,
the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is hidden in the cave of this living being.
One who is free from desire sees him, free from sorrow,
through the grace of the Creator, [beholding] the majesty of the Lord.
I know this undecaying, ancient one,
the Self of all, all-pervading due to his omnipresence,
of whom the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> declare
the cessation of birth — they declare him eternal.
Thus ends the third chapter.
Chapter Four.
He who is one, without color, by the manifold application of his power
distributes many colors for a hidden purpose,

children.text: vi caiti cānte viśvam ādau sa devaḥ
children.translated_text: and into whom all dissolves at the end and from whom all emerges at the beginning — that God,
may he endow us with auspicious understanding.
That indeed is <s>Agni</s> (fire), that is <s>Āditya</s> (the sun),
that is <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), and that is the moon;
that indeed is the pure, that is <s>Brahman</s>,
that is the waters, that is <s>Prajāpati</s> (lord of creatures).
You are woman, you are man,
you are the youth and also the maiden;
you, as an old man, totter with a staff;
you, once born, become the universe-facing one.
You are the dark butterfly, the green parrot, the red-eyed [lightning],
the lightning-pregnant [cloud], the seasons, the oceans;
you, without beginning, abide through omnipresence,
from whom all the worlds are born.
The one unborn (<s>ajā</s>) [<s>Prakṛti</s>], red, white, and black,
producing many offspring of similar form —
one unborn (<s>aja</s>) [<s>Puruṣa</s>], delighting, lies with her;
another unborn (<s>aja</s>) abandons her when her enjoyments are exhausted.
Two birds, companions, inseparable friends,
cling to the same tree.
One of them eats the sweet <s>pippala</s> fruit;
the other, not eating, merely looks on.
On the same tree, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, submerged,
grieves, deluded by helplessness.
But when he sees the other, the worshipped Lord,
and his majesty, he becomes free from sorrow.
In the imperishable, supreme heaven where the <s>Ṛc</s> verses [dwell],
wherein all the gods are seated —

children.text: yas taṃ na veda kim ṛcā kariṣyati
children.translated_text: he who does not know that, what will the <s>Ṛc</s> do for him?

children.text: ya it tad vidus ta ime samāsate [*18]
children.translated_text: Those who know that — they are the ones seated here [in bliss].
The sacred meters, the sacrifices, the rituals, the vows,

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ yac ca vedā vadanti
children.translated_text: the past, the future, and what the <s>Vedas</s> declare —
from this, the wielder of <s>Māyā</s> projects this entire universe,
and in it the other [the individual soul] is confined by <s>Māyā</s>.
Know <s>Māyā</s> to be <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature),
and the wielder of <s>Māyā</s> to be <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord);
by the parts that constitute him,
this entire world is pervaded.
He who alone presides over every womb,

children.text: yasminn idam saṃ ca vicaiti sarvam
children.translated_text: in whom all this comes together and dissolves —
knowing that Lord, the boon-granting, adorable God,
one attains this peace supreme.
He who is the source and origin of the gods,
the lord of all, <s>Rudra</s>, the great seer,
who beheld <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo) being born —
may he endow us with auspicious understanding.
He who is the sovereign of the gods,
in whom the worlds are established,
who rules over this two-footed and four-footed —
to which God shall we offer our oblation?
Subtler than the subtle, in the midst of chaos,
the creator of the universe, of manifold form,
the one encompasser of the universe —
knowing <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious One), one attains peace supreme.
He alone, in time, is the protector of the world,
the lord of all, hidden in all beings;
in whom the <s>Brahma-ṛṣis</s> and the gods are united —
knowing him thus, one cuts the bonds of death.
Like the cream that is exceedingly subtle, above the butter,
knowing <s>Śiva</s>, hidden in all beings,
the one encompasser of the universe —
knowing that God, one is released from all bonds.
This God, the maker of all (<s>Viśvakarman</s>), the great Self,
is ever seated in the hearts of beings;
by the heart, by insight, by the mind is he conceived —

children.text: ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
children.translated_text: those who know this become immortal.

children.text: yadātamas tan na divā na rātrir
children.translated_text: When there is no darkness, there is neither day nor night,

children.text: na san na cāsac chiva eva kevalaḥ
children.translated_text: neither being nor non-being — <s>Śiva</s> alone, the absolute;
that is the imperishable, that is the adorable light of <s>Savitṛ</s>,
and from that has the ancient wisdom proceeded.
Not above, not across,
not in the middle has anyone grasped him;
there is no likeness of him
whose name is Great Glory.
His form does not stand within the range of sight;
no one sees him with the eye.
Those who, through the heart, through the mind, know him
as dwelling in the heart — they become immortal.
'He is unborn' — thus, someone
in fear approaches [him for refuge].
O <s>Rudra</s>, by your auspicious face,
protect me forever.

children.text: mā nas toke tanaye mā na āyuṣi
children.translated_text: Do not harm us in our children, in our descendants, in our life-span,

children.text: mā no goṣu mā na aśveṣu rīriṣaḥ
children.translated_text: in our cattle, in our horses — do not injure us.
O <s>Rudra</s>, enraged, do not slay our heroes;
with oblations we ever invoke you.
Thus ends the fourth chapter.
Chapter Five.
Two [principles] — knowledge and ignorance — hidden in the supreme, infinite <s>Brahman</s>,
are deposited where they are concealed.

children.text: kṣaraṃ tv avidyā hy amṛtaṃ tu vidyā
children.translated_text: Ignorance is perishable, but knowledge is immortal;
he who rules over both knowledge and ignorance is another.
He who alone presides over every womb,
over all forms and all sources —

children.text: ṛṣiṃ prasūtaṃ kapilaṃ yas tam agre
children.translated_text: the sage <s>Kapila</s>, who was born first and whom he
sustained with knowledge at the beginning — him may he behold being born.
Spreading each net in manifold ways,
this God withdraws it in this field;
having created again, the Lord, the sovereign,
the great Self, exercises complete lordship over all.

children.text: sarvā diśa ūrdhvam adhaś ca tiryak
children.translated_text: In all directions — above, below, and across —
illuminating, he shines like the magnificent sun;
thus that adorable, blessed God,
alone presides over the natures of all sources.
He who is the source of the universe, who matures what has its own nature,
and who would transform all that is to be matured,
who alone presides over this entire universe,
and who would assign all the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) —
that which is hidden in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the secret of the <s>Vedas</s>,
<s>Brahmā</s> knows that as the source of <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: ye pūrvaṃ devā ṛṣayaś ca tad vidus
children.translated_text: those gods and sages who knew it in ancient times,
they, becoming one with it, became immortal indeed.
He who, endowed with qualities, is the doer of fruit-bearing actions,
and the enjoyer of what he himself has done,
he, of universal form, possessing three <s>guṇas</s>, treading three paths,
the lord of the life-breath, wanders according to his own deeds.
Of the measure of a thumb, with a form like the sun,
endowed with volition and ego-sense,
with the quality of intellect and the quality of the self,
he is seen as another, even of the size of a needle-point.
A hundredth part of the tip of a hair,
divided again a hundredfold —
such is the size of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), it is to be known,
and it is fit for infinity.
He is neither woman nor man,
nor is he a neuter;
whatever body he assumes,
with that he becomes associated.
Through the delusion of thought, touch, and sight,
through food, water, and rain, through self-growth and birth,
the embodied one, following his deeds in due order,
assumes forms in [various] stations.
Gross and subtle, and many too,
the embodied one chooses forms according to his own qualities;
the cause of his union with these, through the qualities of action
and qualities of the self — another [cause] is also seen.
Without beginning and without end, in the midst of chaos,
the creator of the universe, of manifold form,
the one encompasser of the universe —
knowing that God, one is released from all bonds.
He who is to be grasped through devotion, called the 'nestless' one,
the auspicious (<s>Śiva</s>) one who brings about existence and non-existence,
the God who creates the emanation of parts —
those who know him abandon the body [attaining liberation].
Thus ends the fifth chapter.
Chapter Six.
Some sages speak of inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>),
others, deluded, speak of time (<s>kāla</s>);
but it is the greatness of God in the world
by which this wheel of <s>Brahman</s> revolves.
He by whom all this is ever enveloped —
the knower, the maker of time, endowed with qualities, all-knowing —
ruled by him, this work of creation revolves,
which is to be contemplated as earth, water, fire, air, and space.
Having performed that work and withdrawn again,
having entered into union with principle after principle,
with one, with two, with three, or with eight,
and with time also, and with the subtle qualities of the self,
undertaking actions endowed with <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
and assigning all states of being —
in their absence, there is the destruction of [accumulated] action;
upon the exhaustion of action, he goes forth as another from [mere] reality.
He is the beginning, the efficient cause of conjunction,
seen as beyond the three times, without parts;
worship first that adorable God
of universal form, who has become all beings, who dwells in one's own mind.
He is beyond the tree, time, and [all visible] forms — the other,
from whom this manifest world revolves;
the bringer of <s>dharma</s>, the remover of sin, the lord of prosperity —
knowing him as dwelling in the Self, the immortal, the foundation of all.
Him, the supreme great Lord among lords,
him, the supreme deity among deities,
the supreme master among masters, transcendent —
let us know that God, the lord of the worlds, the adorable one.

children.text: na tasya kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ca vidyate
children.translated_text: He has no effect to accomplish, nor any instrument;
none is seen equal to him or greater;
his supreme power is heard of as manifold,
inherent — [consisting of] knowledge, strength, and action.

children.text: na tasya kaścit patir asti loke
children.translated_text: No one in the world is His master,

children.text: na ceśitā naiva ca tasya liṅgam
children.translated_text: nor is there any ruler over Him, nor any distinguishing mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of His.
He is the cause, the lord of the lords of the sense organs;

children.text: na cāsya kaścij janitā na cādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: and there is no progenitor of His, nor any overlord.
Like a spider, with threads
born from <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature), by His own nature,
the one God covers Himself.
May He grant us absorption into <s>Brahman</s>.
The one God, hidden in all beings,
all-pervading, the inner self (<s>antarātman</s>) of all beings,
the overseer of actions, the abode of all beings,
the witness, the conscious one, absolute, and without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>).
The one controller of the many who are inactive,
who makes the one seed manifold —
those wise ones who perceive Him as dwelling within the self,
to them belongs eternal happiness, and not to others.
The eternal among the eternals, the conscious among the conscious,
the one among the many, who fulfills [their] desires —
that cause, attainable through <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>,
knowing that God, one is freed from all bonds.

children.text: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candra-tārakaṃ
children.translated_text: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars,
nor do these lightnings shine — how then this fire?
Him alone, as He shines, everything shines after;
by His radiance, all this is illuminated.
The one <s>Haṃsa</s> (swan/supreme self) in the midst of this world,
He indeed is the fire that has entered into the waters.
By knowing Him alone, one crosses beyond death;
there is no other path for going [to liberation].
He is the maker of all, the knower of all, self-born (<s>ātmayoni</s>),
the knower, the maker of time, possessing qualities, the all-knower,
the lord of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature) and the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower), the master of the <s>guṇas</s>,
the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), liberation, continuance, and bondage.
He who is of that nature, immortal, established as the Lord,
the knower, all-pervading, the protector of this world,
who rules over this universe eternally —
no other cause is found for [His] sovereignty.
He who first creates <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: yo vai vedāṃś ca prahiṇoti tasmai
children.translated_text: and who indeed delivers the <s>Vedas</s> to him —
to that God, who is the light of one's own <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect),
I, desiring liberation, take refuge.
Without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>), without action (<s>niṣkriya</s>), peaceful (<s>śānta</s>),
without blemish (<s>niravadya</s>), without stain (<s>nirañjana</s>),
the supreme bridge to immortality,
like a fire whose fuel has been consumed.
When human beings shall roll up space
like a piece of leather,
then, without knowing God,
there will be an end to suffering.
By the power of austerity (<s>tapas</s>) and by the grace of God,
<s>Śvetāśvatara</s>, then, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>,
to those beyond the stages of life (<s>āśramins</s>), the supremely pure [teaching],
he proclaimed — [a teaching] cherished by the assembly of true sages.
The supreme secret in the <s>Vedānta</s>,
which was taught in a former age,
should not be given to one who is not tranquil,
nor to one who is not a son or a disciple.
For one who has supreme devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to God,
and as to God, so to the teacher (<s>guru</s>),
to that great soul, these teachings
that have been declared shine forth.

children.text:
oṃ saha nāv avatu saha nau bhunaktu saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai
tejasvi nāvadhītam astu mā vidviṣāvahai
children.translated_text: Oṃ. May He protect us both. May He nourish us both. May we both work together with vigor. May our study be brilliant. May we not hate each other.
Oṃ. Peace, peace, peace.
Thus ends the sixth chapter.
